h1: Srisuksant Urban Krabi — an industrial-design budget hotel closest to Krabi Airport
intro: If you have an early-morning flight out of Krabi, or you land late and don't want a long ride into town — Srisuksant Urban is the name independent travelers bring up as a budget stay that's one of the closest to Krabi Airport (KBV) · It's a small 3-star hotel with industrial design on Phetkasem Road in the Nuea Khlong subdistrict, just about 3 kilometers from the airport, or roughly a 5–10 min drive · The 3-storey building has only 18 rooms, very clean with comfy beds, an on-site restaurant, free parking, a 24-hour front desk, and an airport transfer service · The thing to understand is that there's no swimming pool here and it isn't next to a beach or the town center — it sells value and airport convenience above all · Scores 8.4 from 35 reviews · From about THB 900/night.

body.html: Who Srisuksant Urban is right for — to put it as briefly as possible, Srisuksant Urban is a hotel for people who care about the words "near Krabi Airport" more than anything else · It isn't a beachfront resort in Ao Nang, and it isn't a hotel in the middle of Krabi town where you step out and find food everywhere — it's a small industrial-design budget hotel in the Nuea Khlong subdistrict that positions itself as Krabi's "transit stay near the airport" · It sits on Phetkasem Road, just about 3 kilometers from Krabi International Airport (KBV), or roughly a 5–10 min drive — far closer than hotels in Krabi town or on the Ao Nang side · It opened within the past few years; the 3-storey building has just 18 rooms, which keeps the atmosphere quiet and friendly · Real reviews on Traveloka, TripAdvisor, Agoda, and Booking.com line up on who this place suits: travelers with very early flights out of Krabi, people who land late and want to get to bed quickly without a long ride, road-trippers who drive themselves and want free parking, and anyone using Krabi as a connection point to another province · On the flip side, if you want to walk out your door straight to the sea, a night market, or restaurants, this may not be the answer, because the Nuea Khlong subdistrict is a quiet suburban area that isn't next to the main attractions · But in the role of a "clean budget hotel near the airport," Srisuksant Urban does its job well at an affordable price, and the 8.4 score confirms that most people who come with expectations that match what the hotel is leave satisfied.

Location and getting around — the location of Srisuksant Urban is both its number-one selling point and the thing to get right · The hotel sits at 98 Moo 2 Phetkasem Road, Nuea Khlong subdistrict, Nuea Khlong district, an area on the main route out of Krabi Airport · The biggest draw is that it's just about 3 kilometers from Krabi International Airport (KBV), or roughly a 5–10 min drive, which is very close compared with hotels in Krabi town (about 15 kilometers away) or on the Ao Nang beach side (about 25–30 kilometers away) · For people on early flights, staying here means more sleep and no need to wake up in the dark for a long drive · Many real reviews say the same thing — staff help arrange an early-morning airport transfer, which puts anyone worried about missing a flight at ease · Another point reviews mention is that the hotel is near a market and a 7-Eleven, so finding basic food and supplies isn't a hassle · The honest caveat is that the Nuea Khlong subdistrict is a fairly quiet suburban area that isn't next to a beach or the town center, so if you're heading into Krabi town (about 15 kilometers, or a 20–25 min drive), to Chao Fah Pier to take a boat to the islands, or to Ao Nang beach (about a 25–30 min drive), you need to plan for transport · Anyone without their own car should be ready to call a Grab or use the hotel's car service, because public transport in this area is limited · In short, this location "wins hands down" on the airport, but "trades" being in the heart of the tourist zone for it.

"We landed in the evening, the ride to the hotel took under ten minutes, and we went straight to bed without a tiring long drive into town · On the morning of our flight back the staff arranged a car to the airport right on time · The room was very clean and the bed was comfier than the price suggests — the only thing is there aren't many restaurants around, so prepare a little."

Room types and decor — Srisuksant Urban is a small hotel with just 18 rooms across a 3-storey building, so there isn't a complicated range to choose from, but it focuses on doing the basics well at a budget price · The main room is the Superior Room, available with either one large bed (Double) or two single beds (Twin), which suits both couples and pairs of friends · What makes this place distinctive is its industrial design, playing with exposed-concrete walls, gray-black tones, and simple modern furniture, which makes the rooms look more current than the usual budget hotels in the same area · Many real reviews praise the rooms as "spacious and modern" and "comfy bed with practical furnishings" — meaning roomy, fresh-looking, and with furniture that works well in practice · Every room has air conditioning, a TV, a fridge, a private bathroom with a water heater, and free Wi-Fi · Some rooms have a balcony or windows that let in natural light · The most-praised point in reviews is the cleanliness, which several platforms rate especially high (Traveloka gives cleanliness about 8.8 and TripAdvisor a full 5), and sleep quality (about 4.7/5 on TripAdvisor), because it's quiet and set a fair distance from the main road · The soft, comfy bed comes up again and again · The honest thing to know is that, being a small industrial-design hotel, the rooms lean clean and minimal-cool rather than the warm luxury of a resort, and there's no sea or mountain view — they're designed to "sleep comfortably and cleanly" more than to spend the whole day in.

Facilities (no swimming pool) — let's be straight from the start: Srisuksant Urban has no swimming pool, which is worth knowing before you book, because many people who see the word "Krabi" may expect a pool or the sea · This is a small transit hotel, so its facilities focus on the essentials done well rather than a full resort lineup · What it has includes an on-site restaurant with breakfast service, a 24-hour front desk that matters a lot for late check-ins or pre-dawn check-outs to catch a flight, free private parking that's a real advantage for self-drivers and rental-car users, luggage storage that's handy when you've checked out but still have time before your flight, a shared lounge, a shared balcony/terrace, and free Wi-Fi · The highlight reviewers mention most is the airport transfer service, which many used and were impressed by, especially the pre-dawn runs · Besides the pool, what's missing is a gym and a spa, which is normal for a hotel this size · In short, as a budget stay near the airport, the facilities here "fit the job" — everything a transit guest needs — but anyone after a pool or in-hotel activities should pick somewhere else.

Food and nearby restaurants — the hotel has an on-site restaurant serving simple dishes and offers breakfast (some room rates include breakfast, some charge about 150 baht per person extra — check when booking) · Reviews on the food are fairly middling — the food category on Traveloka sits at about 7.6, lower than the others, reflecting that food is "okay" rather than a selling point · The honest caveat, and the one mentioned most in reviews, is that there aren't many restaurant options around the hotel, because it's in the suburban Nuea Khlong area, not a downtown or beachfront spot · Some international reviews say outright that "the only downside was the lack of a restaurant" — meaning the main drawback is not having many restaurants within walking distance · The good news is the hotel is near a market and a 7-Eleven, so you can grab basic food and supplies, and there are local eateries scattered along Phetkasem Road within a short drive · So many people pick up food on the way from the airport or before checking in, and use the hotel mainly as a place to sleep · In short, measured purely on dining in and around the hotel, it's okay and not a strength, but if you plan your meals ahead (buy food in town, or ask staff to recommend a spot) it's no problem for a one- or two-night transit stay.

Service — service is another point that earns steady praise in real reviews, and one reason the overall score lands in the good range · The point mentioned most is that the staff are friendly and helpful — many reviews use "lovely staff" and "friendly, helpful," especially about arranging the pre-dawn airport transfer in time for flights · The service category on TripAdvisor sits at about 4.7/5, which is high · The 24-hour front desk helps with late check-ins and giving travel info, so people who land late or fly early can plan their next steps more easily · Luggage storage and help hailing a car are also points guests mention positively · But to be fair, some voices in reviews note that the attentiveness isn't consistent every time, with one review saying, in effect, that staff at certain times didn't pay as much attention to guests as they should · That's the normal picture for a small hotel with a limited team, where service quality depends on whoever is on each shift · Overall, if you set expectations to match the hotel's size and price, the service here passes comfortably and is a point most people rate positively.

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — pulling from Traveloka (8.4 from 35 reviews), TripAdvisor (4.0 out of 5 · #3 of 5 B&B-type stays in Nuea Khlong), Agoda, and Booking.com, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: a location that's one of the closest to Krabi Airport, great for early flights and late arrivals; very clean rooms (cleanliness scores especially high); comfy beds and easy sleep thanks to the quiet; industrial design that looks fresh and more modern than the price; friendly staff who help arrange the pre-dawn airport transfer; free parking; and overall value that many sum up as "for this price, getting a clean room near the airport is worth it" · On the watch-out side: the most-mentioned points are no swimming pool, and few restaurants around the hotel, so you have to sort out food or drive out to find it · Next is the distance from the town center and the beach (Ao Nang about a 25–30 min drive, the town about a 20–25 min drive), which makes it unsuitable for anyone who wants to tour Krabi without a car; the staff's attentiveness being inconsistent at certain times; and the in-hotel food being only okay · Almost all of these gripes are about "setting expectations to match the hotel's role" rather than quality problems that keep people from coming back · We should also say honestly that the number of online reviews is still small (Traveloka 35 reviews · TripAdvisor 11 reviews), so it's worth reading the latest reviews before deciding.

"The room was very clean, like new, with cool exposed-concrete design and a comfy bed, and the price wasn't expensive · Perfect for the night before an early flight, because it's so close to the airport · The only gripes are no pool and not many restaurants around, so we bought food from 7-Eleven to eat in the room."

Price comparison and value — the starting price for a Superior room is about THB 900/night at regular rates (we've seen lower during promos or low season, and there have been reports of around THB 1,500 at peak), rising with the season and demand · Compared with other budget stays in Krabi, what makes Srisuksant Urban especially good value is the cleanliness, the fresh-looking design, and the closest-to-the-airport location · Compared with budget hotels in Krabi town such as City Hotel Krabi or Krabi Golden Hill Hotel at similar prices, Srisuksant Urban "wins" on distance to the airport (in town it's about 15 kilometers, but here it's just about 3 kilometers) and on how new the rooms feel, but "loses" on access to the market, restaurants, and the island-boat pier in the town center · Compared with staying on the Ao Nang side, which starts pricier and is farther from the airport, this place saves both on the room and on travel costs on your flight day · In short, if your trip has a night where you need to "sleep near the airport" — whether the first night when you land late, or the last night before an early flight — the money you spend on Srisuksant Urban pays off in extra sleep and peace of mind about your flight · But if you use it as a base to tour Krabi for the whole trip without a car, the value drops because you'll pay for travel into town and to the beach every day.

What to know before booking — a few things make the stay smoother · One, make the most of the near-airport location by staying here on the night you land late or before an early flight, and tell the front desk in advance to arrange the airport transfer (about 250 baht during the day and about 350 baht for late-night to pre-dawn runs) · Two, sort out food ahead of time, because there aren't many restaurants around the hotel — buy food from the nearby market or 7-Eleven, or ask staff to recommend a spot · Three, if you don't have your own car, plan your travel, because it's about a 20–25 min drive into town and about a 25–30 min drive to Ao Nang, so be ready to call a Grab or use the hotel's car service · Four, check on breakfast when booking, because some room rates don't include breakfast (about 150 baht per person extra) · Five, don't expect a swimming pool or a sea view, because this is a transit hotel in a suburban area — if you want a pool or a beach, choose the Ao Nang side or a resort with a pool instead · Six, put the 24-hour front desk and luggage storage to good use for late check-ins, pre-dawn check-outs, and storing bags while you wait for your flight · Seven, since the number of online reviews is still small, it's worth reading the latest reviews to see the current condition before deciding.

Verdict — from all the real reviews, Srisuksant Urban is the hotel that suits people who want a clean budget stay as close to Krabi Airport as possible, especially on the night they land late or before an early flight, and people who drive themselves or use Krabi as a connection point · The especially high cleanliness scores, comfy beds, fresh-looking industrial design, free parking, 24-hour front desk, and well-praised airport transfer make it a worthwhile transit choice at this price · But you have to accept honestly that this place has no swimming pool, isn't next to a beach or the town center, and has few restaurants around the hotel, so it isn't right for anyone who wants the hotel as a base to tour Krabi for the whole trip without a car · If you're after a beachfront resort, a pool, or a central downtown location, this isn't the answer and you should look at the Ao Nang side or the town center instead · But for the role it was designed for — "sleeping comfortably and cleanly near the airport at a light price" — Srisuksant Urban is a tidy fit, and that's why it scores 8.4 from guests who come with expectations that match what the hotel is.

honestSummary: Srisuksant Urban is the best hotel for people who want a clean budget stay as close to Krabi Airport as possible, especially on the night they land late or before an early flight — just about 3 km from the airport, very clean rooms, comfy beds, fresh-looking industrial design, and an airport transfer · But you have to accept that there's no swimming pool, it isn't next to a beach or the town center, and there are few restaurants around the hotel, so it suits a transit stay more than a base for the whole trip.
honestChecks: If you want a swimming pool or a sea view — there's no pool here and it's in the suburban Nuea Khlong area, not by a beach → consider a resort on the Ao Nang side or a stay with a pool instead.

If you don't have your own car and want to tour Krabi for the whole trip — the town is about 15 km away and Ao Nang about a 25–30 min drive, with few restaurants around → be ready to call a Grab / use the hotel car, or pick a stay in the town center.

If you want resort-level service and in-hotel activities — this is a small 18-room hotel focused on transit stays, with no gym/spa and service that's inconsistent at times → set your expectations on cleanliness and closeness to the airport above all.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Srisuksant Urban Krabi

faq.q: How far is Srisuksant Urban from Krabi Airport?
faq.a: Very close · The hotel is on Phetkasem Road in the Nuea Khlong subdistrict, just about 3 kilometers from Krabi International Airport (KBV), or roughly a 5–10 min drive · It's one of the closest stays to Krabi Airport, great for the night you land late or before a very early flight · The hotel has an airport transfer service (about 250 baht daytime · about 350 baht late-night to pre-dawn).

faq.q: Does Srisuksant Urban have a swimming pool?
faq.a: No swimming pool · This is a small 18-room budget hotel focused on its role as a transit stay near the airport, so its facilities cover the essentials — restaurant, free parking, and a 24-hour front desk · If you want a swimming pool or a sea view, consider a resort on the Ao Nang side or a stay with a pool instead.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Srisuksant Urban · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 900/night for a Superior room at regular rates (at peak there have been reports of around THB 1,500) · The main room is the Superior Room, available with either a large bed (Double) or two single beds (Twin) · Every room has air conditioning, a TV, a fridge, a private bathroom with a water heater, and free Wi-Fi · It's worth comparing prices on Agoda and Trip.com and choosing free cancellation before booking.

faq.q: Who is Srisuksant Urban right for?
faq.a: It's great for travelers with very early flights out of Krabi, people who land late and want to get to bed quickly, self-drivers, and people using Krabi as a connection point · The rooms are very clean, the beds are comfy, and it's the closest to the airport at a budget price · If you want a base to tour Krabi for the whole trip without a car, or you want a pool and a beach, the town center or Ao Nang side may suit you better.

faq.q: Are there restaurants around Srisuksant Urban · how do you get into town?
faq.a: There aren't many restaurants around the hotel, because it's in the suburban Nuea Khlong area · There's a market and a 7-Eleven nearby for basic food and supplies, and local eateries on Phetkasem Road within a short drive · Getting into Krabi town (about 15 km · a 20–25 min drive) and to Ao Nang beach (about a 25–30 min drive) requires a car — if you don't have your own car, be ready to call a Grab or use the hotel's car service.

faq.q: Does Srisuksant Urban have breakfast and parking?
faq.a: It has an on-site restaurant and breakfast service (some room rates don't include breakfast and charge about 150 baht per person extra — check when booking) · For parking, there's free private parking, an advantage for self-drivers and rental-car users · There's a 24-hour front desk and luggage storage for guests who have checked out but are still waiting for a flight.
